offense_class: Serious Misdemeanor (first); Aggravated Misdemeanor (second); Class D Felony (third+)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle in Iowa
While under the influence of alcohol or a drug or combination thereof
Or with a BAC of .08 or higher
mandatory_minimum: 48 hours imprisonment or community service (first); 7 days (second); 30 days (third)
enhancements: BAC .15 or higher (increased mandatory minimum)
Second offense within 12 years (Aggravated Misdemeanor)
Third or subsequent offense (Class D Felony)
OWI causing serious injury (Class D Felony under § 321J.2(2)(c))
OWI causing death (Class B Felony under § 321J.2(2)(c))
notes: Iowa uses 'OWI' (Operating While Intoxicated). Implied consent under § 321J.6. License revocation 180 days (first), 1-2 years (second), 6 years (third). Iowa counts all prior OWI convictions regardless of age — no washout period.

offense_class: Serious Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle while intoxicated
BAC .08 or higher, or impairment proven
No prior OWI convictions
mandatory_minimum: 48 hours imprisonment or community service; substance abuse evaluation; drinking drivers course
enhancements: BAC .15 or higher (additional mandatory minimum)
Minor passenger (additional penalties)
notes: First offense OWI is a serious misdemeanor. License revocation 180 days. Temporary restricted license may be available after 30 days with ignition interlock.

offense_class: Aggravated Misdemeanor (second); Class D Felony (third+)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle while intoxicated
Defendant has one or more prior OWI convictions
enhancements: BAC .15 or higher
Prior felony OWI
notes: Iowa has no washout period — all lifetime OWI convictions count. Third offense is a Class D Felony. License revocation 1-2 years (second), 6 years (third+). Barring order for 6 years on third offense.

offense_class: Same as alcohol OWI by offense count
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
While under the influence of a drug or combination of alcohol and drug
Or with any amount of a controlled substance present in the defendant's blood or urine
enhancements: Same enhancements as alcohol OWI apply
notes: Iowa has a per se drug OWI provision — any detectable amount of a controlled substance in blood or urine is sufficient. This includes marijuana metabolites. No impairment showing required for per se violation.

offense_class: Simple Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant drove a vehicle on any highway
In a reckless manner
With willful or wanton disregard for the safety of persons or property
notes: Simple misdemeanor — relatively minor charge. Often used as a plea reduction from OWI. Not an OWI-related offense for enhancement purposes.

statute_title: Duty to Provide Aid and Information — Leaving the Scene
offense_class: Class D Felony (injury/death); Simple Misdemeanor (property under $1,500); Serious Misdemeanor (property $1,500+)
elements: Defendant was the driver of a vehicle involved in an accident
Resulting in injury, death, or property damage
Defendant failed to stop, provide identification, and render aid
enhancements: Resulting in death (Class D Felony)
Resulting in serious injury (Class D Felony)
notes: Leaving the scene with injury/death is a Class D Felony. Property damage only is graded by the dollar amount. Driver must provide name, address, license, and registration.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant unintentionally caused the death of another person
While operating a motor vehicle under the influence of alcohol or drugs
Or while eluding or attempting to elude a pursuing law enforcement vehicle
notes: Class B Felony — one of the most serious motor vehicle offenses. OWI causing death under § 321J.2 may be charged alternatively. Separate from vehicular homicide (reckless driving) under § 707.6A(2).

offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant unintentionally caused the death of another person
While driving recklessly as defined in § 321.277
notes: Class C Felony — applies to vehicular deaths caused by reckless driving without intoxication. Less severe than OWI vehicular homicide (Class B).

statute_title: Operating While License Denied, Suspended, Revoked, or Barred
offense_class: Serious Misdemeanor (OWI-related suspension); Simple Misdemeanor (other suspensions under § 321.218)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle on a public highway
While driving privilege was denied, suspended, revoked, or barred
Defendant had knowledge or notice of the suspension
enhancements: OWI-related suspension carries mandatory jail time
Habitual offender status under § 321.555
notes: OWI-related license suspensions carry mandatory jail time. Non-OWI suspensions are simple misdemeanors. DOT mailing creates presumption of notice.

statute_title: Eluding or Attempting to Elude a Pursuing Law Enforcement Vehicle
offense_class: Aggravated Misdemeanor; Class D Felony (exceeding 25 mph over limit or causing injury)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
While being pursued by a law enforcement vehicle with lights and siren
Defendant willfully failed to stop
enhancements: Exceeding speed limit by 25+ mph during pursuit (Class D Felony)
Causing bodily injury (Class D Felony)
Causing death (Class B Felony)
notes: The pursuing officer must have lights and siren activated. If death results, charged as a Class B Felony (vehicular homicide).

offense_class: Serious Misdemeanor (Schedule I, II, III); Simple Misdemeanor (Schedule IV, V)
penalty_max: 1 year (serious); 30 days (simple); enhanced to Aggravated Misdemeanor or felony with priors
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed a controlled substance
Without a valid prescription or authorization
enhancements: Second offense (Aggravated Misdemeanor)
Third or subsequent offense (Class D Felony)
Possession near school, park, or public housing
notes: Iowa classifies possession by drug schedule. Prior offenses increase the charge level. Drug court and deferred judgment available for first offenders.

offense_class: Serious Misdemeanor (first); Aggravated Misdemeanor (second); Class D Felony (third+)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed marijuana
Without valid medical cannabidiol card
enhancements: Second offense (Aggravated Misdemeanor)
Third or subsequent offense (Class D Felony)
notes: Iowa has not legalized recreational marijuana. Medical cannabidiol program is very limited (low-THC only under § 124E). Any amount of marijuana remains criminal.

offense_class: Serious Misdemeanor (first); Aggravated Misdemeanor (second); Class D Felony (third+)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed cocaine
Without valid prescription
enhancements: Second offense (Aggravated Misdemeanor)
Third or subsequent offense (Class D Felony)
notes: Cocaine is Schedule II in Iowa. Possession is charged under the general possession statute. Crack and powder cocaine treated the same at the state level.

offense_class: Serious Misdemeanor (first); Aggravated Misdemeanor (second); Class D Felony (third+)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed methamphetamine
Without valid prescription
enhancements: Second offense (Aggravated Misdemeanor)
Third or subsequent offense (Class D Felony)
notes: Meth is Schedule II in Iowa. Same possession penalties as other Schedule II substances. Iowa has significant meth enforcement given Midwest prevalence.

statute_title: Manufacture, Delivery, or Possession with Intent — Large Amounts
offense_class: Class B Felony (large amounts); Class C Felony (moderate amounts)
penalty_max: 25 years (Class B); 10 years (Class C); 50 years (repeat or death results)
elements: Defendant manufactured, delivered, or possessed with intent to deliver a controlled substance
In amounts meeting statutory thresholds for Class B or C felony
mandatory_minimum: Mandatory one-third of sentence before parole eligibility (Class B)
enhancements: 5+ kg of marijuana or 100+ kg (Class B Felony)
5+ g of cocaine/meth or specified amounts (Class B Felony)
Death resulting from delivery (Class B Felony with 10-year mandatory minimum)
notes: Iowa's drug trafficking provisions have weight-based tiers. Class B felony drug offenses require serving one-third of the sentence before parole eligibility. Tax stamp violations under § 453B may apply.

statute_title: Manufacturing, Delivery, or Possession with Intent to Deliver
offense_class: Class C Felony (Schedule I/II under threshold); Class D Felony (Schedule III)
elements: Defendant manufactured, delivered, or possessed with intent to deliver a controlled substance
enhancements: Delivery to a minor (enhanced penalty)
Within 1,000 feet of school, park, or public housing (additional 5 years under § 124.401D)
Amount exceeding weight thresholds
notes: Covers distribution below the trafficking thresholds. School zone enhancement adds up to 5 years consecutive. Tax stamp law may add additional charges.

offense_class: Class B Felony (meth or large amounts); Class C Felony (other)
elements: Defendant knowingly manufactured or attempted to manufacture a controlled substance
mandatory_minimum: One-third of sentence before parole eligibility (Class B)
enhancements: Meth manufacturing (Class B Felony)
Manufacturing in presence of minors
Environmental contamination
notes: Meth manufacturing is particularly prosecuted in Iowa. Precursor purchase restrictions under § 124.212A. Environmental remediation costs may be assessed against the defendant.

offense_class: Simple Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed drug paraphernalia
Used or intended for use in manufacturing, testing, packaging, or introducing a controlled substance into the body
enhancements: Delivery of paraphernalia to a minor (Aggravated Misdemeanor under § 124.414(3))
notes: Simple misdemeanor for possession. Selling paraphernalia is a serious misdemeanor. Delivering to a minor is an aggravated misdemeanor.

statute_title: Possession with Intent to Deliver — Schedule I or II
offense_class: Class C Felony; Class B Felony (above weight thresholds)
elements: Defendant possessed a controlled substance
With intent to manufacture or deliver
enhancements: Amount exceeding weight thresholds (Class B Felony)
Near school or park (additional 5 years)
Delivery to a minor
notes: Intent to deliver is inferred from quantity, packaging, scales, baggies, large cash amounts, and other circumstantial evidence.

offense_class: Class A Felony
elements: Defendant committed murder as defined in § 707.1
With premeditation and deliberation
Or while participating in a forcible felony
Or by poison, lying in wait, or torture
mandatory_minimum: Life imprisonment without possibility of parole
notes: Iowa abolished the death penalty in 1965. Life without parole is the mandatory sentence for first-degree murder. No judicial discretion in sentencing.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant committed murder as defined in § 707.1
Not qualifying as first-degree murder
mandatory_minimum: Must serve 70% of sentence before parole eligibility
notes: Second-degree murder is an intentional killing without premeditation, or a killing during certain felonies not qualifying for first-degree. 70% of sentence must be served before parole.

offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
Acting in a sudden, violent, and irresistible passion resulting from serious provocation
By the victim or another person the defendant reasonably believed was responsible
notes: Voluntary manslaughter requires adequate provocation. The provocation must be such as would excite irresistible passion in a reasonable person.

offense_class: Aggravated Misdemeanor; Class D Felony (if public offense)
elements: Defendant unintentionally caused the death of another person
By acting in a manner likely to cause death or serious injury
Or while committing a public offense other than a forcible felony or an escape
enhancements: Commission during a public offense (Class D Felony)
notes: Involuntary manslaughter covers deaths caused by reckless or criminally negligent conduct. Often charged in cases of accidental death during lower-level criminal activity.

statute_title: Assault Causing Serious Injury / Assault with a Dangerous Weapon
offense_class: Class D Felony (serious injury); Class C Felony (dangerous weapon with intent to cause serious injury)
elements: Defendant committed an assault
Causing serious injury to another person
Or used or displayed a dangerous weapon in connection with the assault
enhancements: Intent to cause serious injury with a dangerous weapon (Class C Felony)
Resulting in serious injury (Class D Felony minimum)
notes: Iowa defines assault broadly under § 708.1 to include threats, attempted battery, and completed battery. Aggravated assault elevates by injury severity and weapon use.

offense_class: Simple Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant committed an act intended to cause pain or injury
Or placed another in fear of immediate physical contact that would be injurious or offensive
enhancements: Causing bodily injury (Serious Misdemeanor)
Against a peace officer or other protected person (enhanced)
notes: Simple assault without injury is a simple misdemeanor. Iowa's assault definition includes both threats (putting in fear) and completed battery (physical contact).

offense_class: Serious Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant committed an assault
Resulting in bodily injury to another person
enhancements: Serious injury (Class D Felony)
Use of dangerous weapon (Class D or C Felony)
notes: Iowa combines assault and battery into a single 'assault' statute. Assault causing bodily injury is the equivalent of misdemeanor battery in other states.

offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant had the intent to commit a theft
And in carrying out the theft or in attempting to escape
Did any of the following: committed an assault, threatened force, or threatened purpose
enhancements: Purporting to be armed or actually armed (First-Degree Robbery)
notes: Second-degree robbery is the base robbery offense. Any taking by force or threat of force qualifies. No weapon needed.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant committed robbery as defined in § 711.1
While armed with a dangerous weapon
Or purposely inflicting or attempting to inflict serious injury
mandatory_minimum: Must serve 70% of sentence before parole eligibility
notes: First-degree robbery requires a weapon or serious injury. 70% of the sentence must be served before parole eligibility. Purporting to be armed (even if not) is sufficient.

offense_class: Class A Felony (first degree); Class B Felony (second degree); Class C Felony (third degree)
elements: Defendant confined, removed, or held another person by force, intimidation, fraud, or stealth
With intent to hold for ransom, as a shield or hostage, to commit another crime, or to inflict injury or sexual abuse
mandatory_minimum: Life without parole (first degree); 70% before parole (second degree)
enhancements: Victim suffers serious injury (First Degree under § 710.2)
Ransom or sexual abuse intent (First Degree)
notes: First-degree kidnapping is a Class A Felony with mandatory life without parole. Third-degree kidnapping (§ 710.4) covers less serious confinement offenses.

offense_class: Class B Felony (first degree — occupied); Class C Felony (second degree — unoccupied building); Class D Felony (third degree — property)
elements: Defendant set fire to or burned, or caused to be burned, or aided in the burning of property
Intentionally and without consent of the owner
enhancements: Occupied structure (First Degree — Class B Felony)
Resulting in death or serious injury
notes: First-degree arson requires an occupied structure. Second degree is an unoccupied building. Third degree is other property valued over $200.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant intended to commit murder
And did some act toward the commission of murder
mandatory_minimum: Must serve 70% of sentence before parole eligibility
notes: Attempted murder is specifically codified as a Class B Felony. The 70% mandatory minimum before parole eligibility applies.

statute_title: Assault with a Dangerous Weapon — Intent to Cause Serious Injury
offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant assaulted another person
While using or displaying a dangerous weapon
With the intent to cause serious injury
notes: Assault with a dangerous weapon without intent to cause serious injury is a Class D Felony under § 708.2(2). The intent to cause serious injury elevates it to Class C.

offense_class: Simple Misdemeanor (under $300); Serious Misdemeanor ($300-$749); Aggravated Misdemeanor ($750-$9,999); Class D Felony ($10,000-$14,999); Class C Felony ($15,000+)
penalty_max: 30 days (simple); 1 year (serious); 2 years (aggravated); 5 years (Class D); 10 years (Class C)
elements: Defendant took, obtained, or exerted control over the property of another
With the intent to deprive the other person of the property
enhancements: Value-based escalation through five tiers
Theft from a person (automatic Serious Misdemeanor minimum)
notes: Iowa's theft statute consolidates larceny, embezzlement, false pretenses, and other theft-type offenses. Five tiers based on property value.

offense_class: Class D Felony ($10,000-$14,999); Class C Felony ($15,000+)
elements: Defendant took, obtained, or exerted control over property of another
With intent to deprive
Value of property exceeds $10,000
enhancements: Value $15,000+ (Class C Felony)
notes: Iowa does not use the term 'grand theft.' These are felony theft charges based on the value thresholds in the unified theft statute.

offense_class: Simple Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant took, obtained, or exerted control over property of another
With intent to deprive
Value of property is under $300
enhancements: Prior theft conviction increases degree
notes: Fifth-degree theft is Iowa's lowest theft charge. Often used for shoplifting under $300. Diversion may be available for first offenders.

offense_class: Same as theft by value: Simple Misdemeanor to Class C Felony
elements: Defendant concealed or took possession of merchandise displayed for sale
With intent to deprive the merchant of the merchandise without paying
enhancements: Value-based escalation same as general theft
Organized retail theft (enhanced)
notes: Shoplifting is charged under the general theft statute. Merchants may also pursue civil penalties under § 537.5002 (civil demand for treble damages, minimum $50).

offense_class: Class B Felony (first degree — occupied); Class C Felony (second degree — unoccupied); Class D Felony (third degree)
elements: Defendant entered an occupied structure without permission
With the intent to commit a felony, assault, or theft
enhancements: Occupied structure with persons present (First Degree — Class B Felony)
Armed with a dangerous weapon or explosive (First Degree)
Inflicting bodily injury (First Degree)
notes: Iowa burglary requires entry into an 'occupied structure' — any building, vehicle, or place for overnight accommodation. Intent must exist at time of entry.

statute_title: Burglary in the First Degree — Occupied Dwelling
offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant entered an occupied structure that is a dwelling
While persons are present
With intent to commit a felony, assault, or theft
mandatory_minimum: Must serve 70% of sentence before parole eligibility
notes: First-degree burglary of an occupied dwelling is the most serious burglary charge. 70% minimum before parole. Applies when people are present during the entry.

offense_class: Class D Felony (most vehicles); Class C Felony ($15,000+)
elements: Defendant took, obtained, or exerted control over a motor vehicle of another
With intent to deprive the owner
enhancements: Value $15,000+ (Class C Felony)
notes: Motor vehicle theft is charged under the general theft statute based on vehicle value. Operating a vehicle without consent under § 714.7 is a lesser charge (Aggravated Misdemeanor).

offense_class: Same degree as theft based on value
elements: Defendant received, retained, or disposed of property of another
Knowing it had been stolen
With intent to deprive the owner
enhancements: Value-based escalation same as theft
notes: Receiving stolen property is included in Iowa's consolidated theft statute. The 'knowing' element can be proved by circumstantial evidence.

offense_class: Simple Misdemeanor (under $300); Serious Misdemeanor ($300-$749); Aggravated Misdemeanor ($750-$9,999); Class D Felony ($10,000+)
elements: Defendant knowingly damaged, defaced, altered, or destroyed property of another
Without the consent of the owner
enhancements: Damage amount determines charge level
Graffiti (restitution for cleanup)
notes: Iowa's criminal mischief statute covers all property damage/vandalism. Same value tiers as theft. Restitution typically ordered.

offense_class: Simple Misdemeanor; Serious Misdemeanor (dwelling or habitable structure)
elements: Defendant entered or remained upon the property of another
Without justification
After being notified to leave or knowing entry was forbidden
enhancements: Dwelling or habitable structure (Serious Misdemeanor)
notes: Notice requirement — must be actual or posted notice. Trespass on agricultural land has specific provisions under § 716.7(2)(a)(4).

offense_class: Same as vandalism — value-based tiers
penalty_max: Same as vandalism by value tier
fine_max: Same as vandalism by value tier
elements: Defendant knowingly damaged, defaced, altered, or destroyed property of another
Without the consent of the owner
enhancements: Same as vandalism entry
notes: Criminal mischief is Iowa's statutory term for vandalism/property destruction. Same statute and provisions as the vandalism entry.

offense_class: Simple Misdemeanor (first without injury); Serious Misdemeanor (bodily injury or second offense); Aggravated Misdemeanor (injury with intent or serious injury); Class D Felony (third+ or strangulation)
elements: Defendant committed an assault as defined in § 708.1
Against a family or household member as defined in § 236.2
enhancements: Bodily injury (Serious Misdemeanor)
Injury with intent to cause serious injury (Aggravated Misdemeanor)
Third or subsequent offense (Class D Felony)
Strangulation or impeding breathing (Class D Felony)
notes: Iowa has a specific domestic abuse assault statute. Mandatory arrest when officer has probable cause. No-contact orders automatically issued. Batterer's education program typically required.

statute_title: Domestic Abuse Assault Causing Bodily Injury
offense_class: Serious Misdemeanor; Aggravated Misdemeanor (intent to cause serious injury)
elements: Defendant committed an assault against a family or household member
Resulting in bodily injury
enhancements: Intent to cause serious injury (Aggravated Misdemeanor)
Causing serious injury (Aggravated Misdemeanor)
Use of weapon (additional charges)
notes: Domestic abuse assault causing bodily injury is a serious misdemeanor. Federal firearms prohibition applies (18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(9)).

offense_class: Aggravated Misdemeanor (no injury); Class D Felony (bodily injury); Class C Felony (serious injury); Class B Felony (death)
penalty_max: 2 years (aggravated); 5 years (Class D); 10 years (Class C); 25 years (Class B)
elements: Defendant was a parent, guardian, or person having custody or control of a child
Defendant knowingly acted in a manner that created a substantial risk to the child's physical, mental, or emotional health or safety
enhancements: Resulting in bodily injury (Class D Felony)
Resulting in serious injury (Class C Felony)
Resulting in death (Class B Felony)
Involving manufacture or possession of meth in presence of child
notes: Iowa's child endangerment statute is broad — covers physical abuse, neglect, drug exposure, and other reckless conduct. DHS involvement typically accompanies criminal charges.

offense_class: Aggravated Misdemeanor to Class B Felony based on injury
penalty_max: 2 years (no injury); 5 years (bodily injury); 10 years (serious injury); 25 years (death)
elements: Defendant committed an act which resulted in physical injury to a child
Or knowingly allowed a child to be placed in a situation likely to result in physical injury
enhancements: Resulting in serious injury (Class C Felony)
Resulting in death (Class B Felony)
notes: Physical child abuse is charged under the child endangerment statute. Iowa uses a mandatory reporter system — certain professionals must report suspected child abuse.

statute_title: Violation of a Protective Order — Contempt
offense_class: Simple Misdemeanor (first); Serious Misdemeanor (second+); may also be charged as contempt
elements: A no-contact or protective order was issued
Defendant had knowledge of the order
Defendant willfully violated the order
enhancements: Second violation (Serious Misdemeanor with 7-day mandatory minimum)
Third+ violation (Serious Misdemeanor with 30-day mandatory minimum)
notes: Iowa treats protective order violations seriously with escalating mandatory minimums. Both criminal charges and contempt of court may apply simultaneously.

offense_class: Aggravated Misdemeanor (first); Class D Felony (second or with weapon or protective order in effect)
elements: Defendant purposefully engaged in a course of conduct directed at a specific person
That would cause a reasonable person to feel terrorized, frightened, intimidated, or threatened
And the person actually felt that way
enhancements: Second or subsequent offense (Class D Felony)
While carrying a dangerous weapon (Class D Felony)
Protective order in effect (Class D Felony)
Violation of conditions of bail (Class D Felony)
notes: Stalking requires a 'course of conduct' — at least two acts. Includes cyberstalking. Protective order typically issued upon arrest.

offense_class: Simple Misdemeanor; Aggravated Misdemeanor (third+ in same household or threat of serious bodily injury)
elements: Defendant, with the intent to intimidate, annoy, or alarm another person
Communicated a threat to commit a violent act, or made repeated unwanted communications, or engaged in a course of conduct to harass
enhancements: Third or subsequent in same household (Aggravated Misdemeanor)
Threat of serious bodily injury (Aggravated Misdemeanor)
notes: Harassment in Iowa includes threatening communications, unwanted contact, and repeated annoying behavior. Cyberbullying provisions also exist.

offense_class: Class C Felony (exploitation of $10,000+); Class D Felony ($200-$9,999); Aggravated Misdemeanor (other abuse)
elements: Defendant committed physical abuse, neglect, or exploitation
Against a dependent adult as defined in § 235B.2
enhancements: Financial exploitation over $10,000 (Class C Felony)
Causing serious injury (enhanced)
notes: Iowa has a mandatory reporter system for dependent adult abuse. DHS investigates. Criminal charges may be filed in addition to civil protective measures.

offense_class: Aggravated Misdemeanor; Class D Felony (concealed weapon, felon, or dangerous weapon)
elements: Defendant went armed with a dangerous weapon concealed on or about the person
Or carried a firearm of any kind on or about the person
Without a valid professional or nonprofessional permit to carry weapons
enhancements: Carrying a dangerous weapon (Class D Felony)
On school grounds (enhanced)
notes: Iowa's permit-to-carry system. As of 2021, Iowa is a 'shall issue' state with a permitless carry law (HF 756). However, prohibited persons still may not carry.

statute_title: Felon in Possession of a Firearm
offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant possessed, received, transported, or caused to be transported a firearm or offensive weapon
Defendant is a person convicted of a felony
notes: Applies to persons convicted of any felony in any jurisdiction. Includes constructive possession. Federal felon-in-possession charges (18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(1)) may also apply.

statute_title: Carrying a Concealed Weapon — Prohibited Person
offense_class: Aggravated Misdemeanor; Class D Felony (prohibited person)
elements: Defendant carried a concealed weapon
Defendant is a prohibited person (felon, domestic abuser, subject of protective order)
notes: With Iowa's 2021 permitless carry law, this primarily applies to prohibited persons. Minors under 21 carrying a handgun in public without a permit may also be charged.

offense_class: Aggravated Misdemeanor; Class D Felony (causing injury)
elements: Defendant intentionally discharged a firearm
In a reckless manner
Creating a substantial risk of death or serious injury
enhancements: Causing bodily injury (Class D Felony)
Discharging at an occupied structure
notes: Covers reckless discharge of firearms within city limits, into the air, or toward occupied structures. Additional city ordinances may apply.

offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly and without authorization used, transferred, or obtained the personal identification information of another person
With intent to obtain credit, property, services, or other benefit
enhancements: Victims over 60 or disabled (enhanced penalties)
Large financial loss
Multiple victims
notes: Iowa's identity theft statute covers use of SSN, driver's license, bank account numbers, and other personal identifiers. Restitution typically ordered.

offense_class: Same as theft by value — Simple Misdemeanor to Class C Felony
elements: Defendant had lawful access to or possession of property of another
Defendant misappropriated or converted the property to personal use
With intent to deprive the owner
enhancements: Same value-based tiers as theft
notes: Embezzlement is charged under Iowa's unified theft statute as 'theft by misappropriation.' Common in employer-employee and fiduciary relationships.

offense_class: Class D Felony (negotiable instruments, government documents); Aggravated Misdemeanor (other documents)
elements: Defendant, with intent to defraud or injure anyone
Made, completed, executed, authenticated, issued, or transferred a writing
Knowing the writing to be false or forged
enhancements: Government documents or negotiable instruments (Class D Felony)
notes: Forgery of checks, deeds, and other negotiable instruments is a Class D Felony. Forgery of other documents is an aggravated misdemeanor.

statute_title: Counterfeiting — Forgery of Money or Government Instruments
offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant made, completed, or possessed a forged writing
Purporting to be issued by a government or government agency
With intent to defraud
notes: Primarily a federal crime. State charges under forgery statute are possible for possession of counterfeit currency or forged government documents.

offense_class: Same as theft by value
elements: Defendant issued or delivered a check, draft, or order on a financial institution
Knowing there were insufficient funds or no account to cover it
With intent to defraud
enhancements: Same value-based tiers as theft
notes: Bad checks are charged under the theft statute. Intent may be inferred from failure to make good within 10 days of notice of dishonor.

offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly presented or caused to be presented a false or fraudulent claim for insurance benefits
Or prepared false documentation to support a claim
notes: Iowa Insurance Fraud Bureau investigates. Restitution and civil penalties may be imposed in addition to criminal penalties.

offense_class: Aggravated Misdemeanor; Class D Felony (large amounts or organized activity)
elements: Defendant used a credit card, debit card, or account number
Knowing it was stolen, expired, cancelled, revoked, or without authorization
To obtain money, goods, or services
enhancements: Large amounts or organized fraud ring (Class D Felony)
notes: May also be charged as theft or identity theft depending on circumstances. Online credit card fraud is increasingly common.

offense_class: Class C Felony ($10,000+); Class D Felony (under $10,000)
elements: Defendant knowingly conducted or attempted to conduct a financial transaction
Involving proceeds of specified unlawful activity
With intent to promote the carrying on of specified unlawful activity, or to conceal the nature/source/ownership of the proceeds
enhancements: Amount $10,000+ (Class C Felony)
notes: Iowa's money laundering statute mirrors federal law in structure. Applies to proceeds of any specified unlawful activity.

offense_class: Same as theft by value — Simple Misdemeanor to Class C Felony
elements: Defendant obtained property, services, or other advantage
By means of a false pretense, promise, or representation
With intent to defraud
enhancements: Same value-based tiers as theft
notes: Iowa's general fraud statute. Covers schemes to defraud, false representations, and obtaining property by false pretenses.

statute_title: Sexual Abuse in the First Degree
offense_class: Class A Felony (first degree); Class B Felony (second degree); Class C Felony (third degree)
elements: Defendant committed a sex act by force or against the will of the other person
Or the other person was incapacitated or lacked capacity to consent
First degree: resulting in serious injury or use of a dangerous weapon
mandatory_minimum: Life without parole (first degree); 70% before parole (second degree)
enhancements: Serious injury or weapon (First Degree — Class A)
Aided and abetted (First Degree — Class A)
notes: Iowa uses 'sexual abuse' rather than 'sexual assault.' Three degrees based on force, injury, and victim vulnerability. Sex offender registration required for all degrees.

statute_title: Sexual Abuse in the Second Degree
offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant committed a sex act by force or against the will of another
Aided by one or more persons
Or the victim was under 12
mandatory_minimum: Must serve 70% of sentence before parole eligibility
notes: Second-degree sexual abuse is Iowa's rough equivalent of rape in other states. 70% minimum before parole. Special sentence of lifetime parole supervision upon release.

offense_class: Aggravated Misdemeanor (first); Class D Felony (second+ or in presence of minor)
elements: Defendant knowingly exposed the defendant's genitals or committed a sex act
In the presence of or directed toward a person who is not consenting
enhancements: Second or subsequent offense (Class D Felony)
In presence of a minor (Class D Felony)
notes: First offense is an aggravated misdemeanor. Repeat offenses or exposure to minors is a Class D Felony. May trigger sex offender registration.

offense_class: Aggravated Misdemeanor (first solicitation/patronizing); Class D Felony (second+); Class C Felony (promoting, victim under 18)
elements: Defendant solicited, offered, or agreed to engage in sexual activity in exchange for payment
Or patronized a prostitute
enhancements: Second or subsequent offense (Class D Felony)
Promoting prostitution involving a minor (Class C Felony)
Human trafficking nexus (Class B or C Felony under § 710A.2)
notes: Iowa treats both the buyer and seller as criminal actors. Promoting prostitution (pimping/pandering) is more severely punished. Minors involved in prostitution are treated as victims, not offenders.

offense_class: Class C Felony (possession); Class B Felony (production or distribution)
elements: Defendant knowingly purchased or possessed a depiction of a minor engaged in a prohibited sexual act
Or promoted, sold, or distributed such material
enhancements: Production (Class B Felony)
Distribution (Class B Felony)
notes: Each image or video may be charged as a separate count. Sex offender registration required. Special sentence of lifetime parole supervision applies.

statute_title: Failure to Comply with Sex Offender Registry Requirements
offense_class: Class D Felony; Aggravated Misdemeanor (certain violations)
elements: Defendant is required to register under the sex offender registry
Defendant knowingly failed to register, verify, or update registration information
notes: Iowa's sex offender registry has strict compliance requirements. Must register within 5 business days of any change. Residency restrictions under § 692A.114 apply.

statute_title: Sexual Abuse in the Third Degree — Victim Under Age of Consent
offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant performed a sex act with a person who was 12 to 15 years of age
And the defendant was 4 or more years older
enhancements: Victim under 12 (Second Degree — Class B Felony)
notes: Iowa's age of consent is 16. Third-degree sexual abuse applies when the victim is 12-15 and the defendant is 4+ years older. Victim under 12 is second degree (Class B Felony). Sex offender registration required.

offense_class: Simple Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant engaged in fighting, violent or threatening behavior
Or made loud and raucous noise in the vicinity of a residence or public place
And the conduct tended to provoke a breach of the peace
notes: Simple misdemeanor. Common charge for public disturbances, loud parties, and minor altercations.

offense_class: Simple Misdemeanor; Aggravated Misdemeanor (with weapon, injury, or display of weapon)
elements: Defendant knowingly resisted or obstructed a person known to be a peace officer or other authorized person
In the performance of official duties
enhancements: Use or display of a dangerous weapon (Aggravated Misdemeanor)
Causing bodily injury (Aggravated Misdemeanor)
notes: Iowa uses 'interference with official acts' instead of 'resisting arrest.' Simple misdemeanor unless a weapon is involved or injury results.

offense_class: Aggravated Misdemeanor; Class D Felony (aiding a Class A or B felon)
elements: Defendant, with intent to prevent apprehension or prosecution
Harbored, concealed, warned, or aided a person who had committed a public offense
Or destroyed, altered, or concealed evidence
enhancements: Aiding a person who committed a Class A or B Felony (Class D Felony)
notes: Covers harboring fugitives, evidence tampering, and witness tampering. Separate statute from interference with official acts.

offense_class: Court-imposed sanctions
penalty_max: 6 months for criminal contempt; civil contempt until compliance
elements: A court order existed
Defendant had knowledge of the order
Defendant willfully disobeyed or violated the order
notes: Iowa distinguishes between direct contempt (in the court's presence) and indirect contempt (outside court). Summary punishment for direct contempt; notice and hearing required for indirect.

offense_class: Simple Misdemeanor; Serious Misdemeanor (third+ within 12 months)
elements: Defendant was found in an intoxicated condition in a public place
enhancements: Third or subsequent within 12 months (Serious Misdemeanor)
notes: Simple misdemeanor for first two offenses. Third offense within a year becomes a serious misdemeanor. Officers may transport to a facility instead of jail.

offense_class: Simple Misdemeanor (simple/serious misd case); Aggravated Misdemeanor (aggravated misd/Class D case); Class D Felony (Class A-C felony case)
elements: Defendant was released pending trial on bail or conditions
Defendant failed to appear at required court date
Defendant acted willfully
enhancements: Underlying charge level determines FTA charge level
notes: Failure to appear charge level tracks the seriousness of the underlying case. Bond forfeiture also applies. Bench warrant issued immediately.

statute_title: False Reports to a Public Entity
offense_class: Simple Misdemeanor; Serious Misdemeanor (false emergency report)
elements: Defendant knowingly conveyed or caused to be conveyed a false report to a public entity
Concerning the commission of a crime or emergency
enhancements: False emergency report (Serious Misdemeanor)
notes: Covers false police reports and false emergency calls. False 911 calls (swatting) may be charged as a serious misdemeanor or higher.

offense_class: Class D Felony (threat to commit forcible felony); Aggravated Misdemeanor (other threats)
elements: Defendant threatened to commit a forcible felony or other public offense
Or threatened to commit an act dangerous to human life
With the intent to compel action or inaction, or to intimidate
enhancements: Threat to commit a forcible felony (Class D Felony)
notes: Iowa's threat statute covers both terroristic threats and extortion. Threat must be communicated to the victim or a third party. Anonymous threats are still covered.

offense_class: Class D Felony
elements: Defendant, while under oath or affirmation
Made a false statement material to the issue or matter of inquiry
Knowing the statement to be false
notes: The statement must be material — false statements on immaterial matters are not perjury. Includes sworn testimony, affidavits, and depositions.

offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant offered or gave anything of value to a public official
With intent to influence the official's act, vote, opinion, or judgment
notes: Both the giver and receiver of a bribe may be charged. Class C Felony reflects Iowa's serious treatment of public corruption.

offense_class: Class D Felony (felony custody); Aggravated Misdemeanor (misdemeanor custody)
elements: Defendant was in lawful custody
Defendant escaped or attempted to escape
enhancements: Using force or threat (enhanced)
notes: Escape charge level corresponds to the custody level (felony vs. misdemeanor). Includes walking away from work release or community-based corrections.

offense_class: Simple Misdemeanor (neglect, first); Serious Misdemeanor (abuse, first); Aggravated Misdemeanor (second abuse or torture); Class D Felony (third+)
elements: Defendant knowingly injured, tortured, or destroyed an animal
Or failed to provide food, water, shelter, or veterinary care
enhancements: Torture (Aggravated Misdemeanor)
Third or subsequent offense (Class D Felony)
notes: Iowa's animal cruelty laws have been strengthened but remain controversial due to agricultural exemptions. Livestock managed under standard agricultural practices are generally exempt.

offense_class: Not a new criminal charge — court may revoke probation and impose original sentence
penalty_max: Up to the maximum sentence for the original offense
elements: Defendant was placed on probation
Defendant violated a condition of probation
The violation must be established by a preponderance of the evidence
notes: Iowa uses graduated sanctions for probation violations. Technical violations may result in brief incarceration through administrative sanctions. New criminal conduct may lead to full revocation.

offense_class: Not a new criminal charge — Board of Parole determines consequences
penalty_max: Return to incarceration for remainder of sentence
elements: Defendant was released on parole
Defendant violated a condition of parole
notes: Iowa Board of Parole conducts revocation hearings. Parolee is entitled to counsel. Parole may be revoked, modified, or continued.

offense_class: Same as the underlying offense
elements: Defendant knowingly aided, abetted, or assisted another person in the commission of a public offense
notes: All persons involved in the commission of a public offense are equally liable. The aider need not be present at the scene. Mere knowledge of the crime without participation is insufficient.

offense_class: Generally one class below the completed offense
penalty_max: One class below the completed offense (e.g., attempt Class B = Class C)
elements: Defendant did an act which was a substantial step toward the commission of a public offense
With the specific intent to commit the offense
notes: Iowa generally punishes attempts one class below the completed offense. Attempted murder is specifically codified as a Class B Felony under § 707.11. Renunciation may be a defense.

offense_class: Generally one class below the target offense
penalty_max: Same as the target offense minus one class level
elements: Defendant agreed with one or more persons to commit a public offense
One or more of the conspirators performed an overt act in furtherance of the agreement
notes: Conspiracy requires an agreement and an overt act. Withdrawal before commission of the target offense may be a defense. Conspiracy to commit a Class A Felony is a Class B Felony.
